title: Safe operation and shutdown
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply: safe operation and shutdown

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body:
Learning goal and job context: This lesson teaches safe operation and shutdown for routine cleaning work. Start with the actual job scope, site instructions, manufacturer directions and worker training. Never treat a general lesson as authority to perform restricted or specialist work.

Core procedure: Operate only within training and equipment rating. Route leads away from doors and walkways, use suitable electrical protection and keep liquids away from unrated equipment. Establish a public exclusion zone when needed. Stop and isolate energy before changing accessories or clearing blockages as the manufacturer directs.

Decision-making in the field: Before acting, ask: What is the surface or equipment? What is the soil or hazard? Which product or method is approved? What could harm a person, property or food? If the answer is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.

Worked workplace scenario: A scrubber approaches an occupied corridor. The operator pauses, places barriers and arranges a safe alternative route.

Guided supervised practice: Demonstrate a safe start, cord or battery management, controlled movement, shutdown and isolation on a training machine.

Evidence and feedback: The assessor observes the task and checks whether the learner: uses controls, maintains safe separation and shuts down without exposing bystanders. A learner must explain any unsafe choice, correct it and repeat the demonstration. Record observations, required coaching and reassessment rather than awarding competence from attendance alone.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. Isolation and testing in this lesson apply to portable equipment only, not to a PV system. Electrical testing, isolation and repair of PV systems need a licensed electrician; in Victoria, Energy Safe Victoria guidance supports installation, maintenance and repair by licensed electrical workers, but not testing or who may isolate. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Confirm that the equipment is used only within your training and its equipment rating.
Route leads away from doors and walkways, with suitable electrical protection, and keep liquids away from unrated equipment.
Set up a public exclusion zone when needed.
If the method, product or equipment is unsafe or uncertain, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance before continuing.
Demonstrate a safe start, cord or battery management, and controlled movement on the machine.
Stop and isolate energy before changing accessories or clearing blockages, as the manufacturer directs.
Shut the machine down without exposing bystanders.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Electrical testing, isolation and repair of PV systems need a licensed electrician; in Victoria, Energy Safe Victoria guidance supports installation, maintenance and repair by licensed electrical workers, but not testing or who may isolate. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: Equipment is operated only within training and its rating.
Leads are routed away from doors and walkways, with suitable electrical protection in use.
A public exclusion zone is set up when needed, and liquids are kept away from unrated equipment.
Energy is isolated before accessories are changed or blockages are cleared.
summary: Equipment is operated only within the operator's training and the equipment rating, with leads routed away from doors and walkways.
A public exclusion zone is set up when needed, and liquids are kept away from unrated equipment.
Energy is isolated before accessories are changed or blockages are cleared, as the manufacturer directs.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you check before operating a machine safely?
options: That it runs on any power outlet, including a damaged one and any extension lead that is to hand
That it is used only within training and its equipment rating, with leads routed away from walkways
That leads are laid across doorways to keep them out of the way and the doors are left open
That liquids are kept near the machine so they are ready to use and the wet floor sign is left out

knowledgeChecks.question: What do you do when a scrubber approaches an occupied corridor?
options: Keep going and ask people to move aside and keep the machine on full speed
Speed past the occupied corridor to finish sooner and get the job finished by lunch
Pause, place barriers, and arrange a safe alternative route before continuing
Clear the blockage by hand while the machine is still running today

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say to do before changing accessories or clearing a blockage?
options: Shake the machine to loosen it
Clear it by hand while the machine runs
Stop and isolate energy as the manufacturer directs
